newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian far right may work with EU factions.
newsitem.headline: Austrian far right may work with EU factions.

text.p: Austrian far-right leader Joerg Haider said on Tuesday his party may cooperate with like-minded politicians from other European Union states in the European parliament after elections in Austria next Sunday.

Haider, leader of the nationalist Freedom Party, said he had already had talks with factions within Britain's ruling Conservative Party and Italy's Northern League who are opposed to the Maastricht treaty.
"We are having talks, that's all I'm prepared to say," Austrian news agency APA quoted him as saying at a news conference in Innsbruck.
British Conservatives are split over Britain's future in Europe and separatist Northern League leader Umberto Bossi has called for a revision of the Maastricht treaty.
Austria votes for the first time in elections for the European Parliament on October 13 to select 21 candidates to the Strasbourg-based legislature.
A Vienna municipal poll on the same day looks certain to end half a century of Social Democrat rule in the capital, due to voter frustration at welfare cuts, job losses and tax rises.
The far right is expected to pick up many of the protest votes to nudge it towards the 25 percent mark.

Haider said he would demand fresh negotiations over Austria's net annual EU contribution of around 15 billion schillings ($1.5 billion) if the coalition government parties suffered heavy losses in Sunday's poll.
The controversial leader said he was expecting to better the 22 percent of the vote his party garnered in last December's general election.
